drhp.business: McNally Bharat Engineering is an engineering-led EPC company that designs and executes projects in bulk material handling (coal handling, mineral processing), mineral beneficiation, mining, power, steel, ports and infrastructure, and runs operations & maintenance for plants its customers own. Its business spans the Steel, Power, Port, Infrastructure and Bulk Material Handling segments, where it relies on its engineering design capability, project-management systems and an external vendor and subcontractor base. Management describes the current phase as disciplined rebuilding: selective bidding, executing existing projects and preserving engineering capability after a shrinking workforce and order pipeline.
drhp.end_markets: Steel|Power (conventional and renewable-linked infrastructure)|Ports and logistics|Mining and mineral processing|Infrastructure|Water-related and solar applications (past project experience)|Domestic India (principal focus); historical references in the Middle East and Africa, now pursued selectively
drhp.expansion: No own-capacity expansion is described: the Directors' Report states the Company did not incur any capital expenditure in FY2025-26, and the capital-commitments note states there is no capital commitment at the balance-sheet date. Forward activity is customer-project execution and O&M. Under Coal India First Mile Connectivity work done through JVs, the Sardega (MCL) and Dipka (SECL) coal handling plants finished PG tests in Dec'25 and moved to O&M from 1.1.2026. Chhal and Baroud (SECL) have been in O&M since mid-2024. Ananta OCP (MCL, MBE-AML JV) is targeted for completion by December 2026 after soil-condition delays. Legacy power projects resumed under the resolution plan: at GSECL Bhavnagar, Ball Mill #2A was commissioned in Sept 2025 and Silo #4 was completed in May'26, with the remaining two ball mills and Silos #5-6 targeted by 31.12.2026. DVC Bokaro, suspended since 2018, re-mobilised in May'25 with completion estimated up to March'27. The NMDC/BHEL Nagarnar stacker-reclaimer contract awaits closure with a commercial settlement. The O&M book includes Jindal Stainless (Duburi, ash handling, to 31.12.2028), Adani Kawai (coal handling plant, to 31.12.2026), Adani Raipur (CHP O&M, 01.04.2025-31.03.2028) and Kurmitar Iron Ore (iron ore handling DA-1/DA-2, 01.04.2026-31.03.2036, plus a 33 KV transmission line job, 21.07.2026-20.10.2026). The MD&A also states an effort to scale up O&M business volume by 50% within the next financial year.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Steel sector continues to need investment in capacity, modernisation, material handling and supporting infrastructure.
- Power sector is evolving with changing generation requirements and renewable integration, while conventional power infrastructure still needs engineering and execution capability.
- Development of logistics and port infrastructure creates requirements for handling and moving bulk materials.
- Bulk material handling demand continues across steel, mining, power and ports.
- Infrastructure is an important area of domestic activity but carries extended execution periods, significant working-capital needs and complex contractual interfaces.
- Growth of cloud computing, AI and digital services is raising demand for data-centre infrastructure, with linked power, cooling and utility work.
- India's battery storage market is moving towards larger-scale deployment with increasing tender and auction activity.
- Competition for projects remains high, and execution and working-capital requirements remain important considerations.
- Geopolitical volatility and elevated fuel and energy prices may affect operating costs, business sentiment and EPC demand in 2026-27.
- Tender pipeline comes mainly from established sectors: steel, power, ports, infrastructure, mining, mineral processing and bulk material handling.
- Bidding is selective: tenders are judged on technical suitability, contract terms, customer profile, execution complexity, working-capital needs and risk-return, not size alone.
- The existing order backlog is the base for continuing execution; management focus is on completing existing commitments on time and monitoring costs and cash flows. No order-book figure is disclosed in this text.

Chhal and Baroud (SECL) have been in O&M since mid-2024. Ananta OCP (MCL, MBE-AML JV) is targeted for completion by December 2026 after soil-condition delays. risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The MD&A calls Commercial Qualification for PSU tenders and the ban on MBE by Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd a 'major constraint', linked to net-worth, insolvency and working-capital issues it hopes the Resolution Plan will resolve.
- The Sardega, Dipka, Chhal and Baroud coal handling plants are all in O&M, and for each one the MD&A states 'Negative cash flow for the portion of O&M is matter of concern'.
- The Company says it faced significant challenges with incomplete power projects under threat of BG encashment and rising loan burdens. It resumed work with support from clients such as NTPC, GSEC, DVC and BHEL.
- The MD&A says that over the next few years supplier risk management will be made robust and the Company will try to regain the lost credit line.
- The Ananta OCP CHP faced unfavourable soil conditions from varying overburden and is now targeted for completion by December 2026. The project risk framework covers strategic, operational, financial and hazardous risks.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Disciplined rebuilding and consolidation: strengthen the operating platform, execute available projects, keep financial discipline and pursue new business selectively within established capabilities.
- Marketing: strengthen business development across public and private sectors, where most opportunities come through competitive tendering; prioritise quality of order intake over order volume, weighing contract terms, execution needs, working capital and project risk.
- Talent: strengthen engineering, project-management and operational teams in line with business activity, retaining critical technical capability while staying appropriately sized and cost conscious.
- Technology: leverage engineering knowledge and existing technology relationships in mineral beneficiation, material handling, mining and power; evaluate collaborations with technology providers; apply digital/AI tools in project monitoring, risk assessment, cost control, maintenance and MIS where benefits are measurable.
- Efficiency: tighter control of costs, working capital, project costs and cash flows; early identification of execution issues; maintain an efficient vendor and subcontractor ecosystem.
- Emerging EPC sectors (data centres, battery energy storage, renewable/hybrid energy, green hydrogen) are to be evaluated selectively, with technology partners where needed, as an extension of the core rather than a move away from it.
